description: The chart is a dual‑axis bar chart intended to display two metrics—average accuracy and average token count—for four methods labeled CoT, CoD, CCoT, and CoUT. The categories are arranged along the horizontal axis in two separated groups: the left group corresponds to accuracy (with the title “Accuracy (%)” shown at the top left) and the right group corresponds to token count (with the title “Token Count” shown at the top right). The left vertical axis is labeled implicitly by the title “Accuracy (%)” and uses a linear scale from 70 to 100 with evenly spaced tick marks at 70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, and 100. The right vertical axis corresponds to token count and uses a linear scale from 0 to 800 with tick marks at 0, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, and 800. In the accuracy group, there are four single bars with value labels above them: CoT is shown in red at approximately 91.19, CoD is orange at approximately 80.89, CCoT is light blue at approximately 88.50, and CoUT is green at approximately 88.40. In the token count group, the same four color‑coded methods appear as single bars with value labels: CoT (red) is approximately 676.85, CoD (orange) is approximately 534.24, CCoT (light blue) is approximately 445.91, and CoUT (green) is approximately 354.46. A legend centered below the plot maps colors to method names (CoT, CoD, CCoT, CoUT). The bars are not shown as stacked, and there is no explicit sorting indicated beyond the consistent left‑to‑right method order within each metric group; the only emphasis is the numeric annotation above each bar.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the average accuracy percentages and token counts for four categories: 'CoT', 'CoD', 'CCoT', and 'CoUT', across four benchmarks. The left vertical axis represents accuracy in percentages, ranging from 70% to 100%, while the right vertical axis shows token counts, ranging from 0 to 800. 'CoT' achieves the highest accuracy at 91.19% and has a token count of approximately 676.85. 'CoD' demonstrates a significant decline in accuracy to 75.89%, with a token count of 534.24. 'CCoT' and 'CoUT' exhibit similar accuracy levels, with 'CCoT' slightly outperforming 'CoUT' at 88.50% compared to 88.40%. However, 'CoUT' has the lowest token count at 254.46, indicating a more efficient performance compared to the other categories. The data suggests that while 'CoT' achieves the highest accuracy, 'CoUT' offers a more token-efficient approach, making it a promising alternative for applications requiring lower computational costs.
